# =====================================================================
#  Python build artifacts — NEVER commit these (they are regenerated by
#  the build scripts and are large / machine-specific).  This is what
#  bloated the folder; keeping them out is why the repo stays small.
# =====================================================================
python/build/
python/dist/
python/.venv/
.venv/
__pycache__/
*.py[cod]
*.egg-info/
*.spec.bak

# ---- Workspace data the Python app writes next to itself at runtime ----
#  (The example .mat files in matlab/ are committed on purpose and are
#   NOT matched here — these rules are scoped to the python/ folder.)
python/*.npz
python/reachable_workspace_data_*.mat
python/orientation_workspace_data_*.mat

# =====================================================================
#  Distributable binaries live in GitHub *Releases*, not in git.
#  A one-file VTK exe is typically >100 MB, which exceeds GitHub's
#  per-file limit for normal git anyway — so upload it as a Release asset.
# =====================================================================
*.exe
*.app/
*.AppImage
python/AppDir/
python/.appimagetool-*
#  If you would rather commit the Windows .exe than use Releases, delete
#  the "*.exe" line above.  For files over ~100 MB you must use Git LFS:
#     git lfs install
#     git lfs track "*.exe"

# ================= MATLAB scratch =================
*.asv
*.m~
slprj/

# ================= OS / editor junk =================
.DS_Store
Thumbs.db
desktop.ini
.vscode/
.idea/
*.swp
